title: What If You Boiled Water at the Top of Mount Everest?

scenes.text: What if you boiled water on top of Everest? It would bubble long before it got hot.
At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. At the summit, it boils at around 71.
The air pressure up there is only about 0.325 bar, roughly a third of the pressure at sea level.
Less pressure pushing down means water molecules escape sooner, so the boiling point drops.
Your pot would bubble furiously, with water nearly 30 degrees cooler than a sea level boil.
Anything you cook in it gets less heat. On top of the world, boiling water is not that hot.
